text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing agitation and have a yellowish discoloration of your skin and eyes; could you tell me how long these symptoms have been present and if you have noticed any changes in your urine or stool color?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Viral Hepatitis (likely Hepatitis B given high-risk sexual behaviors and history of recreational drug use).

**Clinical Reasoning:** The patient presents with jaundice and significant agitation. The lab results confirm acute liver injury (elevated Bilirubin, AST, ALT, and INR). The combination of recent high-risk sexual behavior, recreational drug use (which can cause direct hepatotoxicity or act as a vector for transmission), and the exclusion of other causes points strongly toward an acute viral etiology, specifically Hepatitis B or C. The elevated AST and ALT levels are consistent with acute hepatocellular damage. Further testing for Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and Hepatitis C antibody (Anti-HCV) is indicated to confirm the specific viral agent.
